name: CNAME aliases — chain / unresolved target (TDSTS / RFC1034)
description: Follow up to8 owned-session CNAME hops to a declared IPv4/IPv6 answer or synthetic NXDOMAIN. Observe alias/address rewriting without contacting returned addresses. Does not claim cache poisoning, real takeover or security enforcement.

name: DNS answer rotation — rebinding/fast-flux fixture (TDSTS)
description: Alternate configured A or AAAA answers for one owned test name, with TTL0. DNS queries only: the client never connects to the returned addresses. This is a controlled answer-behavior fixture, not an SSRF exploit.

name: Benign controls — long hostnames (TDSTS)
description: Send bounded long, word-like hostnames as a benign comparison corpus. Report observed DNS outcomes; false-positive classification requires independent product events.

name: DNS cache and retries — repeated names (TDSTS / RFC1035)
description: Compare repeated names with unique names and authoritative arrival counts. The controlled receiver supplies the selected TTL. Client attempts and actual upstream delivery remain separate measurements.

name: DNS tunneling — Base32 synthetic transfer (TDSTS / T1048)
description: Measure independent delivery of synthetic bytes through the selected resolver. Uses offset-identified base32 query labels; complete and partial delivery remain distinct from security actions.

name: DNS query labels — custom ASCII (TDSTS / RFC 1035)
description: Send a small, bounded series of operator-entered ASCII labels, including punctuation, under the configured test zone. Captures raw and normalized authoritative observations. This is a query-pattern test, not verified file delivery or proof of detection.

name: Controlled DNS error and recovery observation (TDSTS)
description: Observe bounded normal/error/normal response phases on distinct session-owned names. Synthetic response fixture only; no infrastructure outage, service restart or failover is induced or proved.

name: DGA-like labels — generated names (TDSTS / T1568.002)
description: Generate a bounded reproducible corpus of high-variation labels inside the configured session zone. This evaluates visibility and classification; it does not recreate a malware DGA or register domains.

name: DNS command channel - fixed status / echo
description: Receive a bounded status or echo command in DNS TXT answers and return a matching result digest in DNS questions. Fixed harmless operations only; no arbitrary execution or remote administration. Management coordinates the session separately.

name: DNSSEC — trusted owned-zone probes (TDSTS / RFC4035)
description: Probe separately provisioned signed, bogus and unsigned owned-zone names with DO/CD. Verify direct RRset signatures against a trusted local DNSKEY. Does not construct a root DS chain or authenticate unsigned status; coordinator arrivals indicate misrouting.

name: DNSSEC signatures — valid, invalid, unsigned (TDSTS / RFC4035)
description: Six bounded DO/CD probes against a self-signed lab island, with client-side signature checks. Requires the dnssec extra on both ends. A key learned through the same DNS path is unauthenticated. This fixture does not provision a parent DS chain or establish resolver enforcement; use a separately trusted anchor and provisioned signed zone for that qualification.

name: DNS data transfer — experimental EDNS option (TDSTS / RFC 6891)
description: Measure independent delivery of finite synthetic bytes in local/experimental EDNS option65001. Resolvers may strip unknown options; missing bytes alone are not enforcement.

name: DNS tunneling — encoded subdomains (TDSTS / T1048)
description: Send synthetic data in unique subdomain labels using Base32 or hexadecimal encoding. Independently verify received bytes. A, AAAA and TXT refer to query types; this test does not carry file data in TXT responses. Encoding is not encryption. For DoT/DoH, select the resolver's actual TLS/HTTPS port and trusted certificate identity.

name: DNS file transfer — operator files (TDSTS / T1048)
description: Transfer selected local files through DNS query names or a local/experimental EDNS option in 64-KiB segments. The receiver reconstructs only DNS-observed bytes and independently verifies complete-file SHA-256. Select one ISO or multiple small files. Original TDSTS workload; technique reference MITRE ATT&CK T1048, not a copied exploit.

name: DNS policy — allowed / blocked names (TDSTS / DNS-006,007)
description: Compare configured-policy response codes for two explicit labels in the owned receiver zone. The authoritative fixture answers both normally; the tool changes no product policy. Matching codes do not establish detection or containment.

name: DNS query patterns — beacon / unique labels (TDSTS)
description: Send a bounded sequence of synthetic unique or repetitive labels. Measures receiver observations and DNS responses, without assigning a file-transfer byte count or claiming behavioral detection.

name: DNS rate steps — bounded unique queries (TDSTS / RFC 8198)
description: Compare finite synchronous query stages at operator-selected rates within the global limits. Reports separate client attempts and independent receiver arrivals; no overload threshold, protection or infrastructure-recovery result is inferred.

name: DNS record observations — A / AAAA / NS / MX / SOA / CAA (TDSTS / RFC 1035)
description: Observe finite DNS record queries in the random owned session with synthetic authoritative replies. A/AAAA compare the answer with a known documentation address. Missing or changed answers do not alone prove poisoning, hijacking or containment. No third-party enumeration or zone transfer.

name: Provisioned DNS baseline before and after load
description: Query1–8 separately provisioned relative owned-zone A/AAAA names before and after0–64 synthetic session-owned questions. Compare complete exact-owner address sets; retain missing/error/unattempted observations. Coordinator baseline arrivals mean misrouting. Does not certify general DNS availability or attribute changes to security enforcement.

name: DNS response sizes — bounded ratio fixture (TDSTS / RFC 5358)
description: Measure paired DNS request/response message sizes with finite benign TXT replies in the owned session. The fixture respects a bounded advertised response size. No source spoofing, victim reflection, flood or vulnerability conclusion.

name: Subdomain proliferation with preserved baseline (TDSTS)
description: Observe1–64 new session-owned child names between two known baseline address checks. Synthetic DNS fixture only; no domain compromise or malicious hosting is performed.

name: OS DNS path — synthetic QNAME transfer (TDSTS / T1048)
description: Perform bounded A lookups through the native Windows/Linux name service, preserving its routing and caches. Receiver verifies only actual DNS arrivals. Counters describe logical API calls; wire queries, response codes and selected resolver are unobserved.

name: DNS TXT — response data transfer (TDSTS / T1071.004)
description: Receive a server-generated synthetic fixture through TXT answers. Source bytes are generated only on the receiver; control carries size and hashes. Client verifies each source offset and the complete hash.
